measures.first-answer: A first page (20 answers) of the lab results, asked straight after the import, as an app does to redraw its screen.

scenario.first-answer.says: Asking for a first page of the lab results straight after the import, so the screen can be redrawn.

counts.converts: How many times the Bridge converted a document in this import: 0 where the pod already held the same file, which it knows by the file's hash, so the conversion is skipped; 1 for a file it had not seen.
counts.statements-added: How many statements (one fact each) the files this import wrote hold, not counting the rebuilt view files, which replace what the views held.
counts.versions-added: How many new versions of a record the import wrote: one for each record the source now says differently.
counts.revisions-added: How many new revisions the import wrote: one for each record whose latest version the new document changed. An entry the pod had seen before, unchanged, adds none.
counts.records-added: How many records the pod named for the first time in this import: things the source described that the pod had not met.
counts.entries-changed: How many source entries of the document were edited from the first one: 10 laboratory results for the changed file, a row of that job alone. The row's note says exactly what was edited.
counts.entries-added: How many source entries the document has more than the first one: 1 for the added laboratory result, a row of that job alone.
counts.database-found: 1 if the pod's saved database was beside it when it was opened again, otherwise 0: a process stopped before it closed leaves none, and the pod is then built from every file.
counts.files-read: How many of the pod's files the reopened pod had to read to be built again: every file that holds statements, as the pod's layout says.
counts.statements-read: How many statements those files hold.
